To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the value of capacity is determined by price differences, (ii) prices are determined by the availability of transport capacity and (iii) the availability of storage is an additional determinant of the value of transport capacity.

(1) The value of scarce transport and storage capacity is a function of the temporal and regional price differences; (2) The scarcity of capacity is a function, among others, of the temporal and spatial price differences; (3) The value of capacity is a decreasing function of the capacity size; and (4) The optimal pipeline investment is a function of marginal storage investment and the discounted and aggregated congestion costs over the lifetime's assets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the interdependencies between capacity, capacity value, prices, and investments.
the valuation of natural gas infrastructure capacity and how the scarcity of capacity affects prices.
a better understanding of the interdependencies between nodal prices and the capacity value of storage and pipelines, and how these are influenced by investment decisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the valuation of scarce capacity is a function of prices in the respective residual markets, which, in turn, are determined by supply and demand and the availability of the capacity.
the scarcity of transport capacity, the value of transport capacity and the optimal investment in transport capacity are all related to the scarcity of storage capacity.
the valuation of transport and storage capacity is a complex task and requires a thorough understanding of the underlying market structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the value of scarce capacity and the scarcity itself are determined jointly by the market prices, which in turn depend on the availability of capacity and the investment decisions of all market players.
the value of scarce capacity is a key determinant of the optimal investment in natural gas infrastructure.
in natural gas markets, prices are driven not only by the overall supply and demand but also by the available transport infrastructure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scarcity of storage and pipeline capacity is a key driver of price formation in gas markets.
the value of capacity is not only a function of the marginal cost of capacity but also depends on the cost of congestion.
the scarcity of transport capacity and storages is a major determinant of prices, the value of transport and storage capacity, as well as of the optimal investment size.
